full_judgment:
Md. Altaf Hossain, J.—This appeal is directed against an order dated 10.6.80 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dacca, in Title Suit No. 664 of 1979 of his Court rejecting plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction made in the Suit. The plaintiffs filed the suite for a declaration that the public notice issued by the defendants and published in the local dailies including the Bangladesh Observer on 16.6.79 is not valid, binding and enforceable against the plaintiffs and that the increase in the price of gas made in the aforesaid notification could not be made effective. The plaintiffs on the basis of several contracts with defendant No. 1 became consumers of gas for running their industries. It was stipulated in the contracts that the current rate would be Tk. 9/- per 1000 cft. The contracts provided that in case the company would increase the rite it shall either by publication or by letter posted in the mails give 30 day’s-notice of the change of the price of gas. The consumers might elect to terminate the contract at the end of such period. But the defendant company, in contravention of the terms of the contract has, without giving 30 days notice as required increased the rate of gas to Tk. 16/- per thousand cft. and has issued the impugned public notice. Hence the plaintiffs filed the suit. In the suit, the plaintiffs prayed for a temporary injunction on the allegations, inter alia, that if the plaintiffs were not granted the temporary injunction, the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss inasmuch as their industries will be closed, goodwill will be destroyed employees will be rendered unemployed giving rise to various litigations and causing serious inconveniences to the general public. Plaintiffs' prayer was opposed. The learned Subordinate Judge on hearing the parties an on consideration of their respective cases became of the view that the plaintiffs had no prima facie case and that plaintiffs' loss, if any, could be only pecuniary and rejected plaintiffs' prayer for temporary injunction. 

 2. Being aggrieved, the plaintiffs have preferred this appeal. Mr. K. A. Bakr, the learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiffs submits that the plaintiffs had a prima facie case and the learned Subordinate Judge has erred in law in taking the view that the plaintiffs had no prima facie case. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has also erred in taking the view that the plaintiffs could be compensated in money. 

 3. Mr. Mohammadullah, the learned. Advocate for the respondents, on the other hand, has argued that the plaintiffs have no prima facie case inasmuch as the gas price has been increased in pursuance of directive of the Government which was binding on the defend-ants as well as on the plaintiffs He further submits that it is apparent that the loss complained of by the plaintiffs can be compensated in money. 

 It appears from this clause that change in the price of gas could be effected either by publication or letter giving 30 days notice. In the instant case, the price was changed with retrospective effect and 30 days notice has not been given. It can hardly be disputed that plaintiffs have a prima facie case for getting the declaration prayed for. We refrain from saying anything more at this stage lest this should prejudice any of the parties. The main question in this appeal is whether the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss if the injunction prayed for is not granted. 

 5. The learned Advocate for plaintiffs- appellants have submitted that if the injunction is not granted industries will be closed good-will of the plaintiffs industries will be destroyed the employees of the plaintiffs will be rendered unemployed giving rise to litigations and serious inconveniences. These all aged consequences are evidently remote. The immediate inconvenience would be that the plaintiffs will require to get gas at the enhanced rate. In case the plaintiffs succeed in the suit, they will be at liberty to recover the excess amount paid by them. From this, it is evident that the loss that might occur to the plaintiffs is one which can be compensated in money. The learned Subordinate Judge after considering the cases of the respective parties have come to the conclusion that the alleged injury was remote and may be compensated in money. We do not see any reason to take a different view and to interfere with this finding of the learned Subordinate Judge. 

 6. In the circumstances, though we find, disagreeing with the learned Subordinate Judge, that the plaintiffs have a prima facie case we are of the opinion that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get a, temporary injunction because the injury that the plaintiffs are likely to sustain can be compensated in money.
